title: AquaTerra's 2023 drives: workshops take off · AquaTerra
description: AquaTerra's 2023 drives: {count} drives and {volunteers} volunteer turnouts, mostly children's workshops at Pather Sathi, a plantation run and Merry Miracles.
lede: In 2023 most of AquaTerra's drives became workshops for children, and one place carried much of that work. Across {count} drives, {volunteers} volunteer turnouts and {placesCount} places, the Sunday school at Pather Sathi hosted more drives than anywhere else. June and July were the busiest months, with a numbered plantation run and a long series of art, dance and story workshops.

sections.heading: a sunday school that became the base
body: Pather Sathi hosted more of the year's drives than any other named place, and most of them were Sunday school workshops for children. Colours Of Durga ran as a numbered series from 1.0 on September 23 to 5.0 on October 7. Merry Miracles, a Christmas series of five days from December 15 to 25, had three of its days at Pather Sathi.

The topics ranged widely. Computer basics came in Tech Time, Ctrl+Create and Code and Connect. Science showed up in Wonder Lab and Science Time, art and craft in Soul Sketch and Paper Magic, and story and speaking work in Telling Tales, Once Upon A Voice and Speak to Shine. Each session had its own theme, and many mixed games with making things.

sections.heading: a numbered plantation run
body: The Grow Green plantation drives reached their highest numbers in 2023. The run began in June and ended with Plantation Drive 20.0 at Ashok Hall School on August 27. In July it moved through a cluster of parks and squares in the city, including Gachtala, Goltalab, Gitanjali and Vivekananda Parks and Shubo Malik Square.

Each One Plant One worked with us on drives 9.0 to 12.0, from late June into early July. Across the Grow Green drives that summer, each one planted somewhere between 80 and 100 saplings, and the saplings went into the ground in parks, schools and open spaces.

sections.heading: health checks in the sundarbans
body: The Sundarbans drives in 2023 combined medical care with planting. A medical camp on May 27 recorded more than 100 checkups, Sunderbans Plantation Project 4.0 on June 10 recorded more than 200, and the Pather Sathi Sunderbans Project on July 29 was the fifth edition of that series, with more than 250 checkups.

Volunteers spent time in the Sundarbans on these trips, and each drive's checkup figure belongs to that drive. Across every year AquaTerra has run {sundarbansTrips} Sundarbans trips, and the 2023 trips are part of that longer run.

sections.heading: fundraisers in the middle of the year
body: Fundraisers clustered in the middle of the year. Pride Binge on June 22 was a celebration of stories and solidarity, Match with a Mission was a football fundraiser at VS Arena on July 1, and Full House, an evening of cards at Madhuvan, followed on July 7. Food For All, a food donation drive during Rath Yatra on June 24, served meals to people on the day.

Diwali Night in November was a community fundraiser in Kolkata, with stalls, performances and the people who came along to support it. The formats ranged from football and cards to a Diwali night with stalls, and the year closed with Food Distribution Drive Day 1 at Paradox on December 29, which gave out 60 food packets.

sections.heading: visits to elders
body: Respect and Reach visited the Urban Shelter for the Homeless as a numbered run. It began with drive 1.0 on April 28, continued with drive 2.0 on May 14 and drive 3.0 on May 19, and each visit aimed to look after the elders and support them through kind actions.

Empower Her, a woman awareness camp held on July 14 with the Woman Wings of the Ahamaddiya Muslim Community, was the other outreach event of the middle of the year. Forty women were taught at the camp, which created space for strength, stories and sisterhood.

sections.heading: the last months of the year
body: December was a Christmas run. It opened at Pather Sathi on December 2 with Young Minds, moved through carols and Santa mask making, and included a fold-and-fun origami session at South Calcutta Inner Wheel School on December 12, alongside the five Merry Miracles days.

The months before had their own themes: Durga Puja sessions in September and October, and a Diwali night in November. Together they show a year that kept returning to the Sunday school, the park planting and the same few places across the city.

learnings: Most of the year's drives were workshops for children, so the workshop became the main way AquaTerra worked in 2023.
One place, Pather Sathi, carried the Sunday school series and more drives than any other named place.
The Grow Green run went from June to late August, and the drives moved from one park to the next as the summer went on.
The Sundarbans trips of 2023 paired health checkups with planting, and each drive reported its own checkup figure.
Numbered runs such as Colours Of Durga and Respect and Reach let a reader follow one drive into the next.

faqs.a: In 2023 AquaTerra ran {count} drives and {volunteers} volunteer turnouts across {placesCount} places. Most were workshops for children, many of them at the Sunday school at Pather Sathi, alongside a Grow Green plantation run, Sundarbans medical trips, fundraisers and visits to elders.

faqs.q: Where did AquaTerra hold workshops in 2023?
faqs.a: Pather Sathi hosted more drives than any other named place in 2023, mainly Sunday school workshops. Other places included Ek Tara, School on Wheels in HUHT, the Urban Shelter for the Homeless and Ashok Hall School, where a waste management workshop ran on August 27.

Merry Miracles was a Christmas series of five numbered days from December 15 to 25, 2023. The days covered Christmas crafts at Ek Tara, a dental checkup for children at Gyan Deepak, Santa mask making and a Christmas carnival at the Sunday school, and a movie outing in Shyambazar.

Yes. The Grow Green plantation run in 2023 went from June to August 27, when Plantation Drive 20.0 was held at Ashok Hall School. Drives in parks and squares in Kolkata, such as Gitanjali and Vivekananda Parks and Shubo Malik Square, were part of the run.

faqs.q: Does AquaTerra run health camps in the Sundarbans?
faqs.a: Yes. In 2023 AquaTerra ran a medical camp in the Sundarbans on May 27, Sunderbans Plantation Project 4.0 on June 10 and the Pather Sathi Sunderbans Project on July 29. Their own checkup figures were more than 100, more than 200 and more than 250 respectively.
